title: Normal stalks of relative normalization in a locally Noetherian normal source
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $X$ locally Noetherian (every affine open has a Noetherian section ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume that every stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a domain and integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. For the relative normalization $f.\mathrm{normalization}$ of $Y$ in $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], every stalk is a domain and integrally closed in its fraction field. No integrality or connectedness assumption on $X$ or $Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 035L (lemma-normal-normalization), normality clause, using local Noetherianness for the finite-component hypothesis; proof uses Tags 0357, 0358, 034L.

proof.text: For an affine open V of Y, W=f^{-1}(V) is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, hence Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Each point belongs to only one component: on an affine neighbourhood the minimal primes belonging to components through that point stay distinct upon localization at its prime, whereas its domain stalk has only the zero minimal prime. Thus the components are disjoint. Their complements are finite unions of closed components, so every component W_i is clopen. Domain stalks also make W reduced: a nilpotent section has zero germs everywhere and is zero by the sheaf axiom. Each nonempty W_i is therefore an integral scheme, with integrally closed stalks inherited through its open immersion.

The clopen components give a finite disjoint union W=∐_i W_i, so its sections form the finite product of the section rings B_i. The normalization chart over V=Spec A is Spec of the integral closure of A in this product, by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. This closure is the product of the closures A_i of A in B_i: projection of an integral element is integral; conversely choose one monic annihilating polynomial over A for each coordinate and multiply these finitely many polynomials, obtaining a single monic polynomial annihilating the tuple. For an empty family the product is the zero ring and the chart is empty.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks] to W_i -> V. These maps are qcqs: W_i is clopen in the qcqs W and quasi-compact, and V is affine. Each component normalization is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] and has integrally closed stalks by the cited normal integral source theorem. The chart Spec(product_i A_i) is their disjoint union: the orthogonal coordinate idempotents identify its basic opens with Spec A_i and cover the spectrum. Every stalk in the chart is thus a normal domain, because the inclusion of its component is an open immersion and induces a stalk isomorphism. The affine inverse-image charts cover f.normalization, proving the assertion.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeNormalization_normal_stalks {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hX : ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∀ z : f.normalization, IsDomain (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (f.normalization.presheaf.stalk z)
